subject: Post-demo: Veridian latency vs cost options & POC plan
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.inference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Veridian latency vs cost options & POC plan

Hi Sana — great demo earlier, thanks for the time. Quick written recap and the recommended next steps so we have alignment.

Key stuff we heard from you on the call:
- Expected steady-state: ~20M tokens/month (chat-remix, 2–3 turns typical).
- Peak concurrency: ~60 concurrent users during campaign windows.
- Target latency SLO: p95 between 150–250ms for user-facing flows.
- Initial pilot budget: you mentioned a ballpark but we wanted to qualify range for planning.

Options and trade-offs (high level):
1) Streaming / low-latency tier (hosted API) — best UX, higher unit cost, expected ~ $40–$60 per 1M tokens depending on model and sequence length. Good if p95 <= 200ms is non-negotiable.
2) Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) — middle ground: predictable throughput, ~ $15–$25 per 1M tokens at our standard quantization; lower p95 than batch but depends on pool sizing.
3) Batch / async (throughput-oriented) — lowest cost (~ $7–$12 per 1M tokens) but introduces 200–800ms extra tail depending on batching window and burst profile.

Redwood features that help: SLO-driven routing (can route critical traffic to low-latency variants and costed traffic to batch), automatic prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles to shift unit cost. We can also do canary rollouts and automatic fallback to cheaper model variants during budget pressure.

Attached is a draft mutual action plan (Veridian-MAP-draft.pdf) with a proposed 4-week pilot timeline and the ask for procurement/security contacts.

Questions for you so we can scope pricing & the pilot:
- Can you confirm a monthly budget band for the pilot (e.g., $/month)?
- Which metric should we optimize first: p95 latency or total unit cost ($/1M tokens)?
- Any regulatory/security docs we should queue (SOC2, DSAs, IP commitments)?

Suggested next steps:
1) You confirm budget band + priority metric.
2) We size a 2-week pilot with streaming for critical flows, and a staged switch to dedicated/batch variants for background jobs.
3) Exchange procurement & security contacts; we'll open a HubSpot deal and share a cost-scenario workbook.

Thanks again — available tomorrow 10–11am PT if you want to sync live.

Best,
Logan Wright

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Veridian latency vs cost options & POC plan

Sana — thanks for the quick reply and the priority signal (p95 <=200ms). Below is a concise scenario table (ballpark estimates) to help finance & platform planning. These are conservative ranges; exact numbers depend on model choice, quantization, and average sequence length.

Scenario A — Streaming (hosted low-latency):
- Expected unit cost: $35–$55 per 1M tokens
- Latency: p95 ~120–220ms depending on region and sequence length
- Ops: minimal integration effort; lowest product friction.

Scenario B — Dedicated (reserved pool):
- Expected unit cost: $12–$22 per 1M tokens (committed capacity discounts apply)
- Latency: p95 ~160–300ms depending on pool size and burst profile
- Ops: small onboarding (pool sizing), predictable billing; good middle ground.

Scenario C — Batch / Throughput-optimized:
- Expected unit cost: $7–$11 per 1M tokens
- Latency: addl 200–700ms (can be tuned with batching policy)
- Ops: best for non-interactive workloads or queued background enrichment.

Notes on SLO-driven pricing and routing:
- We do not dynamically bill you higher simply because we route to a lower-latency variant. Pricing is tied to the model variant + deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/batch) + optional premium SLO add-on.
- SLO-driven routing is a policy layer: you can set rules (e.g., route high-priority traffic to streaming tier, automatically fall back to cheaper variant on overload). The add-on for strict enterprise SLOs includes a fallback SLA and longer retention of traces for root-cause analysis.

Recommended pilot (what I propose):
1) 2-week live pilot: streaming for user-facing endpoints + dedicated for mid-priority background flows.
2) Use a dedicated 2-node reserved pool for peak windows to control tail latency; analyze token profile and then evaluate moving non-critical traffic to batch.
3) We'll provide a short cost workbook (attached) with three scenarios mapped to your 20M tokens/month profile.

Attachments: cost-model-3-scenarios.xlsx (7KB stub)

- Confirm procurement contact so we can pre-send SOC2 & DPA.

If that looks good we'll lock the pilot plan and send a short SOW/quote.

Best,
Marissa Cole
